title: Independent finite-volume stationarity refinement
reason: All twelve original L-BFGS-B runs stopped on relative-energy ftol while remaining above the requested projected-gradient tolerance. Preserve those outputs and test the discrete stationarity equations directly.
initial_state_rule: For each charge use its original N1600 independent_gaussian output, without choosing by agreement or gradient size.
method: Newton for the same analytic finite-volume gradient; sparse symmetric local Hessian plus the exact fixed-Q rank-one term, solved by sparse LU and Sherman-Morrison.
preflight: Check analytic Hessian-vector product against two central finite-difference steps of the independently checked gradient on the same N32,L8 interior test as before. Abort refinement if both relative discrepancies exceed 1e-5.
backtracking: Try scale 1,1/2,...,1/1024; project to the original bounds; accept first finite trial that strictly reduces projected-gradient infinity norm, or meets tolerance. Stop and retain failure if none does.
outputs: independent_refinement_results.json, independent_refinement_profiles.npz, independent_refinement_execution.jsonl; original twelve run outputs remain unchanged.
interpretation: A refined root is evidence for a stationary point of the bounded finite-volume radial functional; neither global minimization nor continuum or nonlinear stability follows. Numerical full gradients and core Euler residuals are reported as well as projected gradients.
